entries.guidance: For finite-lifetime moving owned objects that must interact with a target, align both deterministic proof placement and returned Game Spec spawn geometry with the actor proof path. entries.title: Owned-object lifecycle evidence does not require motion

entries.title: Actor-origin evidence requires explicit spatial lineage

entries.title: Recurring schedule proofs require reachable clock steps
entries.guidance: A single advance_time step moves the clock to its endpoint and then dispatches callbacks already due there. A positive-delay callback scheduled during that dispatch is reachable only from a later advance_time step. Prove N recurrences with N separate interval-sized steps, and make exact private-state counters include install-time writes plus only the callbacks reachable from those steps.

evidence.summary: Actual-provider contract scenarios expected spawn_order 1 after one interval even though install plus the due scheduled callback produced 2, and expected 6 after one coarse six-interval advance even though a positive-delay callback rescheduled at the endpoint was not reachable in that same step, producing 2. entries.title: Autonomous first-playable checks do not require a generated action
entries.guidance: When an accepted generated mechanic has the exact autonomous install contract shape, with install as its sole behavior trigger, no logical_action lifecycle callback, and no dispatch_action scenario steps, run first-playable checks without a generated action ID and accept ordinary trusted input-response evidence. Continue to require and authenticate one exact action for action-driven mechanics, and fail closed when an action-driven project loses or conflicts on that action.

evidence.summary: The accepted actual-provider contract was autonomous: behavior trigger install, lifecycle callbacks install and scheduled, no connections, and no dispatch_action scenario steps. entries.title: Contract-required capability use remains source-owned
entries.guidance: When source capability-use validation reports an unused grant, keep the failure at source repair if the accepted contract semantically requires that capability to be used. In particular, state_write is source-required when any scenario's final state_equals value differs from its setup value or the private state's initial value. Preserve the accepted contract and ask source repair to restore the required reachable call; route the failure to contract repair only when the unused authority is not required by accepted contract behavior.

evidence.summary: The accepted contract granted state_read and state_write and required spawn_sequence and active_spawned_hazards to change from setup values. entries.title: Source generation needs private-state transition obligations

Require reachable awaited writes for each final value, preserve endpoint dispatch semantics for coarse advance_time steps, and choose cleanup before recurring creation when the accepted final state returns active lifecycle state to its setup value. Do not expose scenario IDs, unrelated observations, or evaluator-authored assertions.

evidence.summary: The accepted contract required spawn_order and active_hazard_instances to reach different values after one recurrence, three reachable recurrences, and a coarse cleanup boundary. entries.title: Provider transport schemas must mirror source guidance

Keep intentionally excluded data such as full contract scenarios excluded.

entries.title: Contract repairs need one closed invariant checklist
entries.guidance: For every contract repair, recheck required intent capabilities, mandatory lifecycle callbacks, scenario trigger mode, private-state write obligations, and the exact accepted configuration declaration manifest together before returning. For every structurally valid rejected contract candidate, collect intrinsic and reference-validation issues together with accepted-intent lineage and safety issues before producing repair feedback; an earlier validation layer must not mask a later invariant. Preserve the latest rejected candidate's issues as exact failure evidence and separately retain a bounded, deduplicated, provenance-checked history of distinct earlier same-stage issues. Render both sets to repair generation and require every earlier invariant to remain satisfied while correcting current issues. Render the exact required-capability manifest and an exact configuration declaration manifest that preserves every accepted key and default. Use boolean, integer, or number for matching scalar values. Use stable_id for an accepted string only when that exact value occurs in exactly one trusted catalog kind; otherwise use a bounded string. An unknown_reference repair must restore the manifest declaration kind without substituting another default. Autonomous install scenarios must omit dispatch_action and logical_action; logical-action scenarios must retain both. A final state_equals that differs from setup or initial state must retain state_write. Correct the reported paths without changing unrelated checklist items.

entries.title: Source repairs need one closed transition checklist

entries.title: Visible recurrence requires runtime creation evidence
entries.guidance: Do not accept a recurring owned-object mechanic from a scheduled callback declaration, private-state counter transitions, or deterministic evaluator success alone. The external mechanic probe must observe at least two distinct mechanic-owned object creations across separate scheduled intervals in the mounted runtime, then observe expiration or cleanup without unbounded accumulation. Preserve manual gameplay denial when the runtime shows only the initial object even if contract and source artifacts describe recurrence.

evidence.summary: Manual gameplay showed one stationary red hazard and one inert white entity. No additional hazards visibly spawned despite the accepted contract declaring a 1200 millisecond scheduled cadence and deterministic scenarios reporting repeated creation.

An independently positioned autonomous owned-object lifecycle may leave actors empty when it already carries an exact entity reference and has no actor-origin spatial rule. Continue requiring an actor role for bound-entity behavior or explicit actor-origin creation, and reject every nonempty actor or target role not represented by an exact referenced entity.

entry.title: Moving owned objects need position-following target checks
entry.guidance: Query targets around the owned object current observed position on bounded recurring lifecycle checks shorter than its lifetime; reschedule while active and stop after the first hit or expiry.

evidence.summary: Actual source generation repeatedly produced a transient projectile that traveled and was cleaned up but queried and mutated the target at its stationary location immediately after creation, before the owned object could overlap the target. The durable source-generation prompt now requires target queries to follow the owned object's current observed position during scheduled or fixed-step travel, with bounded rescheduling and cleanup after the first hit or expiry.

The source repair preserved owned-object creation, actor origin, travel, and active state, but scheduled the first target query at the full projectile lifetime. The moving object passed the target between observations and targetInteractionsDelta remained zero. The durable mechanic-general source guidance now requires bounded recurring lifecycle checks shorter than the accepted lifetime, with active travel and rescheduling before expiry until the target is reached.

entry.title: Active owned objects must survive post-action observation
entry.guidance: Keep active owned objects observable through the post-action lifecycle check and defer expiry cleanup until after bounded motion and target interaction can be observed.

evidence.summary: Actual source generation created and moved an owned projectile, interacted with the target, and then destroyed it before the post-action observation. The durable mechanic-general source-generation repair guidance now requires active owned objects to remain observable through the post-action lifecycle check, with bounded motion, target interaction, and deferred expiry cleanup.

entry.title: Negative timestamp sentinels must permit the first action
entry.guidance: When a last-action timestamp uses a negative sentinel for no prior action, bypass cooldown on the first accepted action and write the current time only after acceptance.

evidence.summary: The source repair rejected the first logical action because it compared simulation time against a negative initial last-action sentinel as if a prior action existed. The accepted contract initializes last_fire_time_ms to -1, so the first action must bypass cooldown and write the current time only after acceptance. The durable mechanic-general timestamp guidance now makes that sentinel rule explicit and adds it to zero-creation lifecycle repair diagnosis.

The durable mechanic-general source guidance now requires exact target-kind provenance from the accepted target binding and forbids binding IDs or invented object-kind strings in spatial queries.
